result.note: Tested the scrapping of the Parandur airport project and its design and site features; skipped the investor conclave figures and the speculative replacement site.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Tamil Nadu government scrapped a proposed greenfield airport meant to serve as Chennai's second airport. Where was this airport to be built?
questions.explain: Chief Minister Joseph Vijay told the Assembly on 24 August 2026 that the state was scrapping the INR 274 billion Parandur project, a site he had opposed while campaigning. The state has named alternative areas but no final site or timetable.
questions.source: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay told the Assembly on Monday that the state is scrapping the INR 274 billion (USD 2.86 billion) Parandur project, a site he had opposed on the campaign trail before becoming Chief Minister in May.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Parandur airport project, which Tamil Nadu scrapped in August 2026:
items: It was designed to handle 100 million passengers a year.
It had not yet received central clearance when it was scrapped.
Nearly half of the proposed site was irrigated farmland.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the project had central clearance secured, with land acquisition underway and a dedicated metro line planned. It drew sustained farmer protests because nearly half the site was irrigated farmland and about a quarter water bodies.
questions.source: Parandur was designed for 100 million passengers a year, with central clearance secured, land acquisition underway, and a dedicated metro line drawn to reach it.
